# Everyday lines for short clips. H3 Prompt Writer must add nothing to any of them
# and switch nothing off: no sound, music or one-take note, no moved opening or ending.
The man on the left waves while the woman on the right laughs.
The woman waves at the camera.
The girl waves goodbye from the bus window.
The little boy waves both hands and smiles.
The crowd waves their phones in the air.
The old man waves his hat.
She waves at her friend across the street.
He gives a thumbs up and winks.
She nods slowly and looks away.
He shrugs and raises his eyebrows.
She breaks eye contact and looks at the floor.
He points at the sign and laughs.
She runs her fingers through her hair.
He runs a hand over his face.
Her face falls when she reads the message.
She drops her gaze and smiles shyly.
Her eyes flash with anger.
He flashes a peace sign at the camera.
She claps her hands twice.
The audience claps and cheers.
She dances in the kitchen.
The beat drops and everyone jumps.
He breaks into a moonwalk.
They are having a blast on the dance floor.
She is on fire tonight, spinning across the stage.

The lights dim as the band takes the stage.

He drops pasta into boiling water.

She runs the knife under the tap.

The cat walks along the fence.

The sun drops below the horizon.
Night falls over the city.
Evening falls over the harbour.
She climbs the stairs to the rooftop.
They hike up a snowy mountain trail.
She walks through deep snow.
Snow-capped mountains glow in the morning light.
The river runs through the valley.
A waterfall pours into the lake.
She walks in the rain without an umbrella.
It starts raining on the street.
The rain stops and the sun comes out.
A light wind moves the curtains.
Her hair blows in the wind.
A strong wind rips the umbrella from her hand.
The wind dies down and the field goes still.
Wind chimes turn slowly on the porch.
She climbs down the fire escape.
A fire truck races down the street.
Fireworks burst over the bay.
They sit around the campfire and laugh.
The fire goes out and smoke rises.
Police lights flash in the rain.
He runs onto the field.
She jogs through the park.
They train hard at the boxing gym.
He takes one shot at the basket and scores.
She breaks the world record.
The ball smashes into the net.
He kicks the ball into the goal.
The boxer falls to the mat.
She dives into the pool.
He sprints to the finish line.
The skater crashes into the wall.
The runner crosses the line in a flash.
A surfer catches the surf at dawn.
Tears run down her face.
Tears running down his cheeks, he smiles.
A single tear falls from her eye.
She falls to her knees and cries.
His heart races as the car pulls in.
A shiver runs down her spine.
She breaks down crying.
He breaks her heart with one look.
Her mascara runs as she laughs.
She falls in love at first sight.
The color drains from his face and his face goes dark.
She smiles, the memories flash before her eyes.
He feels the cold wind on his face.
Petals fall around the couple.
Confetti falls as they kiss.
Leaves fall from the trees.
Snowflakes fall softly on her coat.
Her silk dress falls to the floor.
The lights flicker and go out.
She turns off the lights.
He switches off the lamp and goes to bed.
The power goes out.
She lights a candle and goes out the back door.
The TV turns to static.
She looks at the TV and turns to her friend.
He stares at the monitor, then turns to the window.
She turns off the TV and sits back.
The screen goes dark.
The sky goes dark as the storm rolls in.
Thunder rumbles in the distance.
Lightning strikes the tower.
A lightning-fast punch knocks him down.
The house explodes.
He opens his eyes and looks at the door.
She slams the door behind her.
The door creaks open.
He knocks on the door.
The window shatters.
Breaking news flashes across the screen.
She breaks the silence with a laugh.
The ice breaks under his feet.
He fires the gun twice.
A siren wails as the police car speeds away.
She takes a photo of the sunset.
The camera flash goes off.
The building is on fire.

A car crashes into the pole.
Her phone drops onto the bed.
Slow push in on her face.

First person view walking down the hallway.
